The Theory of Moral Sentiments, Adam Smith.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/adam-smith/the-theory-of-moral-sentiments

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Adam Smith, the author, died 1790.

First publication of the text used: 1759 (SE colophon: 'The Theory of Moral Sentiments was published in 1759 by Adam Smith.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1759, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (Scotland (first published in London and Edinburgh, 1759; Wikipedia infobox 'The Theory of Moral Sentiments': country Scotland, publishers Andrew Millar, London, and Alexander Kincaid and J. Bell, Edinburgh)): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die did so in 1790, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 1861.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
